title: Module 15 Misconception Sort
intro: Decide whether each statement is true, false, or depends. These are the misconceptions that cost students points on exams.

items.s: Chi-square tests whether the means of categories differ.
A significant chi-square tells you which cells are responsible for the association.
items.why: It says the variables are related. Look at observed against expected counts for the pattern.

items.s: Each person may appear in only one cell of the contingency table.
items.why: Independence of observations is a basic assumption.

items.s: A larger N makes a given proportional difference more likely to be significant.
items.why: Chi-square grows with N when the proportions are held constant.

items.s: An odds ratio and a relative risk are the same thing.
items.why: They are different measures that only approximate each other when the outcome is rare.

items.s: You can run a chi-square test on percentages instead of counts.
A 2 by 2 chi-square with df = 1 and a value of 6.67 is significant at .05.
items.why: The critical value for df = 1 is 3.84.

items.s: Whether a significant chi-square reflects a meaningful relationship
items.why: Report an effect size such as phi, Cramer's V, or the odds ratio, because large samples make small associations significant.
